To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the beneficial associations of physical activity on 2-h but not fasting blood glucose in Australian adults are more evident in men with low waist circumference and in women with high waist circumference.

In the Australian Diabetes, Obesity, and Lifestyle study of 9,214 adults, physical activity was associated with lower levels of 2-h post-load plasma glucose but not with lower levels of fasting plasma glucose.

1) physical activity is associated with lower 2-h PG, but not with FPG in men and women; 2) the association between physical activity and 2-h glucose is stronger in men and women at the extremes of waist circumference than in those with moderate waist circumference; and 3) the association between waist circumference and 2-h post-load glucose was independent of physical activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between physical activity and blood glucose.
understanding the role of physical activity and its association with 2-h glucose in individuals with varying levels of central adiposity.
the association between physical activity and glucose levels in a large population-based sample of men and women in Australia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
physical activity is associated with a reduction in the 2-h PG level, but the relationship is not linear.
physical activity is beneficial for 2-h PG in men and women, regardless of waist circumference.
physical activity is associated with reduced risk of diabetes, but this is more evident for 2-h PG than for FPG.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
physical activity is beneficial to 2-h PG, but not FPG.

the beneficial associations of physical activity on 2-h PG are independent of waist circumference and may help to explain why the benefits of physical activity on type 2 diabetes risk may occur in the absence of weight loss.
the associations between physical activity and glucose levels are not linear, and there is a threshold effect for the beneficial effects of exercise.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 2-h PG, rather than the FPG, should be the preferred measure of glucose homeostasis for the study of physical activity and type 2 diabetes.
the benefits of physical activity are not confined to the obese population.
physical activity is associated with lower 2-h PG, and this effect is present across the waist circumference distribution.
